newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds-S.Korea eyes Q4 soybean/meal deals.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds-S.Korea eyes Q4 soybean/meal deals.

text.p: South Korean feed millers and crushers are expected to buy soybean and soymeal this week for their fourth quarter requirements, prompted by recent sharp declines in Chicago futures, traders said on Monday.
"We expect local buyers to move into the market as current soybean and soymeal prices are close to buyers' target prices," a trader with a Seoul-based feed miller said.

The NLCF is seeking 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for September 30 or October 20 arrival, 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellets for arrival between November and December and 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal for arrival in December.
Traders said NLCF's purchases, if completed, are likely to prompt other South Korean buyers to enter the market for soybean or soymeal.
"If the NLCF buys soymeal, we expect another buyer, the Big Feed Mills, to purchase meal for the same arrival," one said.
Traders said three major South Korean soybean crushers were expected to negotiate privately this week to purchase nearby shipments as prices have fallen to their target levels.

Among the three buyers -- Cheiljedang Corp and Shindongbang Corp would each buy 35,000-50,000 tonnes of soybeans per month for the fourth quarter and Sam Yang Foods Co Ltd would buy 15,000 tonnes, traders said.
Japanese and Taiwanese oilseed buyers are likely to remain sidelined this week, waiting for lower-price new U.S. soybean crop from around October, traders said.
Tokyo traders said that old crop prices are still too high to buy.
"As we've covered enough Brazilian soybean at least until September shipment, there's no urgency to buy now," a soybean trader at a major Japanese trade house said.
"Some traders may buy U.S. soybean only if there's a nearby shortage," the trader added.
